Amir — attaching the technical inventory as discussed. Pulls below (high level):

- Default hosted routing: requests are ingressed in the customer nearest regional edge and routed to the lowest-latency available execution pool that meets policy (region preference, cost tier, model compatibility). Primary execution regions today: us-west-2 (US), us-east-1 (US), eu-west-1 (EU).
- Cross-border: when a request enters with no pinned region, routing may select an execution pool in a different legal region for latency/capacity. We surface this in the Console and allow region pinning and per-route routing policies.
- Subprocessor chain (execution path):
  - Ingress edge (CDN partner — cached request metadata) -> Redwood runtime control plane (control traffic only) -> Execution pool (Redwood-managed compute) -> Optional downstream 3rd-party caching layer (partner) -> Persistent logging/metrics (cloud provider managed).
- Deletion responsibilities:
  - Redwood runtime: owns ephemeral KV/prefix caches and removes model context per customer deletion requests within 48 hours (configurable playbook).
  - Cloud provider: infrastructure-level logs and snapshots follow provider retention; Redwood coordinates deletion requests and validates via deletion receipts from providers where available.
  - Partners (edge/cache): handled via contractual redaction/TTL terms; redacted roster attached.

Attachments in this message: compute_inventory_20271204.csv (CSV), subprocessor_roster_redacted.pdf (PDF), deletion_playbook_excerpt.md (MD).

Notes: the CSV has per-pool region, typical sequence length assumptions, and kernel/quantization profiles we select for cost/latency. If you need physical city-level footprints for providers, we can request a deeper vendor attestation but that takes extra lead time.

Hannah
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
